title: Heterogeneous Fleet Alignment — week notes
content:
Purpose: capture this week's alignment discussion on running a mixed GPU fleet (H100/A100/L4 + preemptible nodes) across regions, decisions we made, experiments to run, and concrete actions. Meet time: 2028-04-11 09:30 PT. Attendees: Jamal (chair), Asha, Liam, Sofia, Marcos, Grace (SRE async), product PM (Evan) joined for 15m.

High-level problem statement
- We are seeing diverging utilization/latency behavior when routing identical workloads to H100 vs A100 in eu-west1 and asia-southeast1. Cost delta is ~1.6x but p50 latency differs based on seq len distribution and kv-cache hit rates.
- Edge/nearby regions (apac-edge nodes running L4) produce good p95 but high variance in throughput due to smaller batch sizes.
- Preemptible pools are significant for batch/low-priority workloads, but preemption spikes in us-west last week caused a subtle tail latency regression for some routed canaries.

New observations (data)
- Warm-start index (WSI): quick heuristic we introduced this week. WSI = fraction of requests that hit prefix/KV cache within first 200ms of request lifecycle. Measured: us-west 0.38, eu-west1 0.52, apac 0.21.
- Kernel autotune telemetry: in-region H100 instances pick different matmul kernels depending on seq_len distribution; eu-west shows 12% better throughput vs us-west for the same model+batch.
- Preemption correlation: 3 of 6 preemption spikes correlated with cloud provider maintenance windows. Preemptible churn increased GPU scheduling jitter by ~18ms p50, ~60ms p95 for long-running primed sessions.

Decisions taken (consensus)
1) Region tagging for routing: mark apac-edge L4 as "low-cost-low-burst" and opt them into only small-seq short-lived requests (<=128 tokens) with strict fallback to A100 for longer seqs.
2) Warm-start aware routing toggle: allow routing policy to prefer regions with WSI >= 0.4 for latency-sensitive routes. Rollout gate: 10% of traffic for 48h then ramp.
3) Preemptible hedging policy: add fractional reserved capacity of 8% in us-west and 5% in eu-west1 for high-priority lanes to cover preemption tail risk.
4) Kernel-autotune capture: capture per-request kernel id and seq_len for three model families (gpt-small, gpt-medium, gpt-large) for 7 days, store in short-retention telemetry dataset.

Experiments to run (owners + timelines)
- Experiment A (Liam): dynamic WSI routing. Implement simple scoring: score = 0.7*WSI + 0.3*(1/cost-index). Run 10% traffic for 48h, compare p50/p95 and cost per 1M tokens. Target start: 2028-04-13. Measurement dashboard: /fleet/metrics/wsi-routing.
- Experiment B (Asha): L4 burst throttling. Limit concurrency for L4 nodes to measured median concurrency (observed 6) and enforce per-node queue depth to reduce variance. Run in apac-edge only. Start: 2028-04-14.
- Experiment C (Sofia): preemptible stagger strategy. When preemption occurs, test an exponential backoff with 100ms base, doubling up to 1s before migration. Simulate on canaries for 72h. Start: 2028-04-15.
- Experiment D (Marcos): kernel autotune logging + kernel fallback policy. Log kernel ids and, if chosen kernel produces >10% higher latency vs fallback, trigger a probe to fallback kernel for subsequent requests for 5m. Start: 2028-04-17.

Risks / open questions
- WSI signal stability: short-retention telemetry may be noisy; need smoothing windows and outlier removal. Who owns smoothing? Proposed: Metrics infra (Grace) to own aggregation logic.
- Cost impact: preferring higher WSI regions may increase cost. PM Evan wants a cost-ROI table before full rollout.
- Safety for canaries: need a quick rollback mechanism if kernel-autotune fallback oscillates and causes thrash.
- Edge cold-starts: L4 nodes see frequent cold containers; investigate lightweight warm pools for the most common workloads to improve WSI without heavy capacity commitment.

Action items (owner — due)
- Asha: implement L4 concurrency cap + dashboard panel for variance (due 2028-04-14).
- Liam: wire WSI into routing policy engine and create canary rollout script (due 2028-04-12 for canary infra, start experiment 2028-04-13).
- Sofia: build preemptible stagger simulation harness and run 72h test (due 2028-04-15 start).
- Marcos: add kernel-id logging to telemetry (7d retention) and a small probe policy in runtime (due 2028-04-17).
- Grace (metrics infra): define smoothing and alert thresholds for WSI (due 2028-04-16).
- Jamal: prepare a short cost/benefit note for PM (Evan) with conservative ranges and rollback criteria (due 2028-04-13).

Notes from PM sync (Evan)
- Product cares about deterministic p95 for the inaugural dedicated-customer alpha in APAC. They are OK with modest cost increases if p95 improves by >=15ms.
- PM requested a kill-switch route config in Console to pin customer traffic to a specific region/model variant during incidents. Product-ops to spec.

Comm plan
- We will paste an executive summary in #infra-updates and link to this doc after first canary runs. If the WSI experiment improves p95 sustainably, plan a short postmortem and runbook update.

Misc
- Quick spike idea: use cached KV fingerprinting at load-balancer to pre-warm KV for expected request prefixes (requires LB change; low priority).
- Noted related tickets: INFRA-3421 (routing policy gaps), LR-2104 (apac L4 cold start investigation), PR-879 (kernel logging plumbing).

Appendix: quick telemetry snippets (raw)
- region, WSI, p50-ms, p95-ms, cost-index
- us-west, 0.38, 18, 64, 1.0
- eu-west1, 0.52, 16, 55, 1.6
- apac-edge, 0.21, 12, 78, 0.46

Next sync: 2028-04-18 09:30 PT. Please update action-item statuses in this doc before then.
